findings.remaining_runtime_risk: A structurally valid Definition could receive conflicting formal interpretations or a stronger non-collapse claim than its evidence supports.
required_evidence: Counterexamples: all references resolved with validation scope absent; unresolved reference without a declared gap; two differently worded statements with the same meaning.
Check interpretation against all three voices and declared neighboring/current definitions; record unsupported source clauses.

findings.remaining_runtime_risk: A matching owner label and valid local signature could be mistaken for an actual semantic-owner determination when new authorization code is added.
required_evidence: A valid local key with a copied definition-owner label is rejected for semantic promotion.
Unbound, rotated or revoked keys cannot make new effects; historical approved effects retain their exact recorded basis.

findings.remaining_runtime_risk: The successor may bind a source digest to document content it did not actually hash. This is a static race possibility, not a reproduced exploit or claim about current admitted data.
required_evidence: Planned controlled writer-interleaving case checks that parsed content always corresponds to the captured digest.
Persistent and transient source changes must cause a clean retry/failure or remain outside the pinned immutable snapshot.
findings.closure_rule: Runtime mitigation is complete only when the selected implementation, required verification and applicable exact owner gates actually finish.

findings.remaining_runtime_risk: Readers may see mixed epochs or fail during cutover; crash recovery could leave authorized records and current lookup inconsistent. Rechecking sources immediately before commit does not prevent a later external write.
required_evidence: Planned reader-during-cutover, competing writer, stale preimage and crash-at-each-publication-step cases.
After recovery, readers see a complete old or complete new selected epoch, or an explicit unavailable state; no mixed state is labeled current.
findings.closure_rule: Runtime mitigation is complete only when the selected implementation, required verification and applicable exact owner gates actually finish.

findings.remaining_runtime_risk: A prospective profile may contain unresolved hashes, use fixture hashes as real outcomes, or require its own future authorization digest. No actual digest cycle is asserted; the design must rule one out.
required_evidence: Fixture-dependent, predicted and observed digests cannot be substituted for each other.
A content-dependency graph distinguishes reviewed inputs, decision evidence and generated outputs; no output must hash itself.
findings.closure_rule: Runtime mitigation is complete only when the selected implementation, required verification and applicable exact owner gates actually finish.

findings.remaining_runtime_risk: The same conceptual record can have different semantic digests, and duplicate-key input can be interpreted differently from the text a reviewer saw. This is a protocol risk, not a reproduced failure of current string-only context epochs.
required_evidence: Planned cross-runtime cases: 1 versus 1.0, exponent forms, negative zero, unsafe integers, Unicode and numeric-looking keys.
Duplicate keys and unsupported nonfinite/precision values fail before review; source text and normalized content remain traceable.
findings.closure_rule: Runtime mitigation is complete only when the selected implementation, required verification and applicable exact owner gates actually finish.

required_evidence: Prototype verification cannot be ready while the realization binding is pending.

required_evidence: Rejected/deferred Product or semantic outcomes never reach their dependent apply effect.
